transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-11 16:00 UTC / Duration: ~52m / Recording: yes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Brooks (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (HelixCare Head of Platform), Sofia Martinez (HelixCare Security Eng), Tom Keller (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick check of SSO progress, audit log export validation, retention window options, and SOC2 artifact request. Action items and due dates captured.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, we have about 50 minutes today, is that still good?
[00:08] Raj Patel: yup perfect, we've got Sofia and Tom on, Sofia is on for the SSO bits.
[00:12] Sofia Martinez: hey all, sorry a bit loud here, dog in the room.
[00:15] Evan Brooks: no worries, we wanted to start with the SSO status then move to audit logs.

[00:32] Maya Chen: quick runthrough — we pushed the SAML metadata yesterday to the test endpoint, Sofia, did you pick that up or do you need us to resend?
[00:40] Sofia Martinez: I saw it, I started config but the NameID format gave me a little grief, some attributes didn't map, might be me or the IdP mapping.
[00:47] Evan Brooks: that's expected, the default mapping uses email as the subject; if your IdP is sending persistentIDs we can flip to the other binding. I'll drop the exact attribute mapping in the notes.

[01:12] Raj Patel: timeline wise we want SSO in test by end of week, compliance wants us to exercise SSO flows before the gate call.
[01:19] Maya Chen: understood. Sofia if you can share the exact test accounts and metadata file we'll do a rapid test — Evan can queue the SSO handshake on our side.
[01:26] Sofia Martinez: I'll share metadata and 3 test accounts (admin, analyst, read-only) by Thursday.

[02:00] Tom Keller: small question on audit logs — our compliance team needs proof that logs are immutable for the retention window, is Redwood append-only or do you support WORM?
[02:12] Evan Brooks: good question. For the hosted pilot we write audit events to an append-only internal store and retention policies are enforced; for Private/VPC customers there is an option to stream to your SIEM or S3, where you can enable object locking (WORM) if needed. I'll put that detail in the SOC2 + logs doc.

[02:48] Sofia Martinez: do you have sample exports? format? Our ingestion pipeline expects a CSV/json with timestamp, actor, action, resource, outcome.
[02:55] Evan Brooks: yes, JSON lines by default, and we can do CSV transformation. We'll send a small sample export today; it will contain fields: ts, user_email, action, model, request_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, lat_ms, outcome.

[03:30] Maya Chen: retention — what window are you targeting for the pilot? Last time you mentioned 90 days but compliance asked about 180.
[03:38] Raj Patel: we're leaning 90 for cost, but compliance wants to see 180 in production. For pilot they may accept 90 if we can demonstrate export to long-term storage.

[03:55] Evan Brooks: that's workable. We can set the pilot to 90 days, plus automatic daily export to an S3 bucket you control for 180+ archival. That keeps the hot store small but gives you immutable archives in your tenant.

[04:12] Sofia Martinez: how about encryption and KMS? If export lands in our S3 we need to manage the KMS keys ourselves.
[04:19] Evan Brooks: yes we support customer-managed keys for exports. For hosted customers we have envelope encryption at rest; for Private we integrate with your KMS/HSM. We'll include KMS notes in the doc.

[05:00] Maya Chen: SOC2 — Tom, do you want the full report or just the summary evidence for now?
[05:07] Tom Keller: summary and the specific controls around logging and access control. We don't need full SOC2 right now but we need evidence that those controls exist and are testable.

[05:15] Maya Chen: we'll share the SOC2 summary and a control matrix that maps to logging and RBAC controls. I'll put that in the drop by Monday.
[05:22] Raj Patel: great. Also a minor item — we're seeing a lot of noisy events in the audit stream, a bunch of token-refresh and telemetry pings that clutter the view. Can we tune that?
[05:30] Evan Brooks: yes, there's a filter layer in the audit pipeline. We can suppress telemetry-only heartbeats and expose a flag for the pilot to turn off debug-level events. We'll push a config change and run a small backfill to show before/after.

[06:00] Sofia Martinez: any chance you can add a field showing dataset_id or tenant_id in each row? makes correlation easier.
[06:07] Evan Brooks: we already include tenant_id in the payload; dataset_id is possible — would you want it surfaced as a separate column or an attribute?
[06:12] Sofia Martinez: separate column please, that maps to our SIEM ingestion.

[06:40] Maya Chen: we'll add that to the sample export. Evan, can you confirm the schema change and send a sample by end of day?
[06:45] Evan Brooks: yes I'll do that.

[07:20] Raj Patel: on RBAC, we want least privilege for the pilot but also a way for operations to escalate for debugging. What's the recommended approach?
[07:28] Evan Brooks: recommended pattern is role-based defaults plus break-glass roles with audit triggers. Break-glass use requires an approval workflow and all activity is flagged. We can demo the workflow if you want.

[08:00] Tom Keller: that sounds good. For the gate we'll need an itemized list of who has break-glass and what justification is required.

[08:20] Maya Chen: I'll assemble a proposed RBAC mapping (admin, ops, analyst, viewer) and tag who we've seen on the call to map to those roles, then you can iterate.

[09:00] Sofia Martinez: small nit on retention policy: if audit is exported daily to S3, do we still pay for hot storage? we don't want unexpected costs during pilot.
[09:09] Evan Brooks: hot store cost is proportional to retention window; if you export daily and set hot retention to 30 days, cost drops significantly. We can provide an estimate sheet with token volumes to show cost delta.

[09:40] Maya Chen: we'll include cost estimates for 30/90/180 day hot retention with export. Raj, you wanted a short bench for latency impact?
[09:49] Raj Patel: yes, we have a production-ish flow that needs sub-200ms median for generate calls. If redenwood adds audit hooks, will that push latency?

[10:00] Evan Brooks: audit logging is async in the path we propose, it shouldn't add to tail latency; we will, however, need to do a quick test to confirm under load. We can run a focused benchmark of your flow.

[10:30] Tom Keller: can we get a short test harness? our SRE wants the script to run in our lab.
[10:36] Evan Brooks: we can provide a small harness and instructions to replay requests and collect latency. Evan (typo) -> I'll make sure it's in the shared folder.

[11:05] Maya Chen: ok let's recap — action owners and dates: I'll send SOC2 + control mapping by 3/15; Evan will send sample audit export with dataset_id column and run export test by 3/19; Sofia will provide IdP metadata and test accounts by 3/18; Raj to confirm retention target by 3/16; Tom to review RBAC by 3/20. Any disagreements?
[11:20] Raj Patel: that's right. Also can we add one more step — schedule a short joint run where we validate SSO login + a small end-to-end request that hits logging and confirm export lands in S3?
[11:30] Maya Chen: yes, we'll schedule a 30-minute run after SSO is configured. Propose 2027-03-22 for the run?
[11:36] Sofia Martinez: that works for me.

[12:00] Evan Brooks: one more note — compliance asked about evidence retention for pilot; do you want us to keep raw logs for an additional 30 days beyond the pilot for audits?
[12:09] Tom Keller: probably not necessary, as long as we can export and show chain-of-custody for the exported artifacts.

[12:45] Maya Chen: ok good. We'll also add a short doc explaining chain-of-custody and how exports are signed/hashed.

[13:10] Raj Patel: competitive note — we looked briefly at Anthropic's hosted offering, they do similar exports but their retention UI is more rigid, so this flexible export + KMS control is important for us.

[13:30] Maya Chen: thanks for that. Anything else on compliance?
[13:34] Sofia Martinez: just to confirm, who will own the export automation? Redwood will provide the Lambda/automation script and we will configure the S3 and KMS?
[13:42] Evan Brooks: correct — we'll provide the automation, you own the destination config and keys.

[14:05] Tom Keller: last question — if we decide to go Private deployment later, will these controls map over easily?
[14:12] Evan Brooks: yes, Private includes the same controls, and gives you the control plane in your VPC; the RBAC and audit schema remain the same. We'll document the delta.

[14:40] Maya Chen: great. I'll send the doc set and SOC2 summary. Evan will send audit sample and run the export test. Sofia will send IdP metadata and accounts. We'll plan the SSO+export validation run on 3/22 and a gate call for compliance on 3/25.

[15:00] Raj Patel: thanks everybody.
[15:02] Sofia Martinez: thanks.
[15:05] Evan Brooks: thanks, chat soon.

End recap (auto): SSO metadata exchange, sample audit export with dataset_id, retention 90 vs 180 decision, SOC2 summary, RBAC mapping, schedule run 2027-03-22, gate call 2027-03-25.

Notes: transcription includes minor mis-hearings, names may be slightly off in spots.
